headline: Local IT Consultant Now Charging Clients 'Premium Airflow Fee' To Compensate For Potential Visa Fee Hike
body:
For software engineer Rajesh Sharma, the news of potentially higher H-1B visa costs has been an opportunity to finally monetize his office environment. Since learning that his future work permit could cost upwards of $100,000, Sharma has begun itemizing his daily workspace expenses, starting with a 'Premium Airflow Contribution' of ₹4,500 per meeting.

'If the cost of doing business is going to be this high, I have to ensure every breath I take in this cubicle is accounted for,' said Sharma, who has also started renting out his ergonomic chair to junior developers during his lunch break. 'I’ve already installed a coin-operated meter on my dual-monitor setup. If a client wants me to debug their code, they aren't just paying for my expertise; they are paying for the electricity used to power the high-resolution pixels of their own salvation.'

His manager at the suburban tech firm has reportedly been supportive of the pivot, noting that the company plans to introduce a 'Latency Surcharge' once the new visa policy takes effect. The office has already replaced the complimentary coffee machine with a tiered subscription model, where employees can choose between 'Standard Caffeine,' 'Project-Delivery Jitters,' or 'Executive-Level Anxiety' at varying price points.

'I think it’s a brilliant market adjustment,' said human resources lead Suman Rao, while adjusting a newly installed toll gate at the office entrance that charges per foot of floor space occupied. 'We are simply teaching our team to treat their presence in the global economy as a rare, luxury commodity. Eventually, we hope to move to a pay-per-keystroke model, which should help cover the cost of everything from visa processing to the annual office Diwali party snack fund.'
caption: When the visa fee hits $100k, you start charging for the oxygen in your cubicle. Adapt, improvise, thrive. #ITLife #H1B #WorkLifeBalance #TechTrends (satire)
igHook: Would you pay a 'Premium Airflow Fee' to keep your current job?
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a modern office desk with a laptop, a partially filled coffee mug, and a small, official-looking plastic sign placed next to the keyboard.

sourceHeadline.title: Trump extends push for $100,000 H-1B visas by another year

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 is the only piece that moves away from the tired, nihilistic 'organ harvesting' trope found in over half the entries. It grounds the absurdity in a believable, mundane corporate setting, using specific details like the 'standard caffeine vs. executive-level anxiety' subscription tiers to create a cohesive world rather than relying on shock value.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses generic, invented names for a satirical take on corporate culture and IT industry challenges. The premise is clearly absurd and hyperbolic, avoiding any real defamatory claims, communal targeting, or identification of specific real-world private individuals.
